::: {#exm-rarity-die}
#### Rarity of the outcomes of a die

<!-- no-figure: the example is two numbers -->

Let $X$ be the roll of a fair six-sided die.
Each [outcome](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/probability-basics.html#def-experiment-outcome)
has [probability](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/probability-basics.html#def-probability) $1/6$.

```{r}
#| label: rarity-die
rarity <- function(p) 1 / p
p_fair <- 1 / 6
p_loaded_six <- 1 / 2
p_loaded_other <- (1 - p_loaded_six) / 5
rarity_fair <- rarity(p_fair)
rarity_loaded_six <- rarity(p_loaded_six)
rarity_loaded_other <- rarity(p_loaded_other)
rarities <- c(
  fair = rarity_fair,
  loaded_six = rarity_loaded_six,
  loaded_other = rarity_loaded_other
)
rarities
```

So each face of the fair die has [rarity](#def-rarity) $\rarityf{x} = `r rarity_fair`$:
one roll in six.

Suppose the die is loaded so that a six has probability $1/2$.
Then $\rarityf{6} = `r rarity_loaded_six`$.
If the other five faces share the rest equally,
each has $\rarityf{x} = `r rarity_loaded_other`$.
The more probable an outcome, the lower its rarity.

:::
